acceptance.criterion_verbatim: hyperlinks clickable, verified against TO-C's measured renderer -- not against the documentation.
acceptance.invocation: TO-C's measurement (tools.py:617/:658 hardcode contentType 'text'; census 8 hits / 71 files) -- no post was made and no Graph call was issued
acceptance.output_evidence: CANNOT BE SATISFIED UNDER D-PROSE, AND THE CRITERION'S OWN WORDING IS WHY. It says verify against TO-C's MEASURED RENDERER rather than against the documentation -- and what TO-C measured is that the send path posts contentType 'text', under which the content is NOT parsed as markup. So a markup hyperlink is not clickable on the current renderer, and no formatting change can make it so: it needs contentType 'html', which is D-HTML, a gateway code change riding safe-ec2-deploy. WHAT THIS TO DOES INSTEAD, and it is a lesser thing stated as one: a SENTENCE-ENDING url is placed ALONE ON ITS LINE, which is the best available form under 'text'. THAT IS NOT A CLICKABILITY CLAIM. Whether the Teams client auto-linkifies a bare url is UNMEASURED -- observable only by posting, which TO-C was explicitly told not to do and did not.
acceptance.denominator: 0 posts made; 0 Graph calls; 2 of 2 send sites confirmed still posting 'text'
acceptance.status_reason: PLANE: renderer/live. NAMED LATER RUN: D-HTML -- the contentType change, built and applied here under Rule 26 on Andrew's separate word, with the gateway-bounce cost stated first. ⛔ AND THIS ROW IS THE WHOLE JUSTIFICATION FOR THE J2 SEQUENCING: had the standard been written before TO-C measured, it would have specified link MARKUP that the renderer discards, and it would have passed review because it matched the documentation. The criterion asks for the renderer, not the docs, precisely so that could not happen. TWO THINGS MUST NOT BE READ INTO THIS ROW: it does not say a bare url is unclickable, and it does not say the formatting is worthless -- D-1 and D-2 are the readability half of Andrew's complaint and they are met.

mutant.description: THREE in-battery mutants plus the checker control. (1) CONSERVATION: a formatter that drops the last three words is shown to FAIL the content_tokens equality -- without it, 'content is never lost' passes for any formatter that happens not to lose anything on one fixture. (2) THE CAP: MAX_SENTENCES_PER_PARAGRAPH raised to 99 leaves the wall of text intact as a wall, restored in a finally -- so the cap test is measuring the cap and not the fixture. (3) FIXTURE CONTROLS: the wall is asserted to violate the cap BEFORE formatting (5 sentences, 1 block) and its url asserted to start out buried mid-line, so neither the cap test nor the url test can pass on an already-compliant input. CHECKER: output_evidence blanked on D-1 in a scratchpad copy, anchor-asserted first.
mutant.expected: Each mutant kills the assertion built for it; the fixture controls fail if the fixtures stop being adversarial; the checker mutant returns rc=1 INVALID naming the mutated row.
mutant.observed:
All three in-battery mutants fire inside a 14-test suite ending OK rc=0. ⛔ AND TWO REAL DEFECTS WERE CAUGHT BY THESE TESTS BEFORE ANY COMMIT, WHICH IS THE POINT OF WRITING THEM AS PROPERTIES: (a) the degenerate-input property FAILED on '


' -- whitespace-only input was returned unchanged and violated the blank-line property; fixed to return ''. (b) THE MORE INTERESTING ONE, WHICH NO PROPERTY CAUGHT: the first implementation hoisted EVERY url, satisfied all seven properties, and produced FRAGMENTED PROSE -- 'Full detail is at' / url / 'if you want the breakdown.' as three paragraphs. It passed its own tests and read WORSE THAN THE WALL IT REPLACED. Caught by printing the output and reading it. The code was narrowed to hoist only sentence-ending urls, and the property was narrowed to match -- with the cost pinned by its own test so the weakening is explicit rather than a quiet relaxation.
